assets.name: bundle-snail
assets.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: actual production drawings for a 2D game creature death animation, not a promotional illustration. Image 1 is the sole approved character design and registered neutral pose. Create a square 2048x2048 transparent PNG, arranged as exactly 2x2 equal 1024x1024 cells, no gutters, borders, captions, labels, letters, scenery, floor, or cast shadows. Each cell contains one complete rendering of THIS SAME left-facing bundle snail at the same pixel scale, camera, palette, and lighting. Treat every cell as the provided 512x512 reference uniformly enlarged exactly 2x; the original foot contact baseline is y896 within each 1024 cell. Preserve generous transparent margins. The round amber-gold spiral shell, spiral direction, two tan mushrooms, three red berries, leaf cargo wrapping, green strap and green outline must be identical in size, construction and arrangement throughout. The shell and cargo form one rigid unit, NEVER squash, stretch, enlarge or redesign them. Retain the mint-ivory smooth muscular foot with subtle cool green shading, original illustrated game-sprite rendering and very dark green outlines. The approved design is small and plump, not realistic or gruesome. Draw these functional death key poses in reading order: TOP LEFT: exact neutral reference, both upright eye stalks and round dark eyes, full soft foot and rear tail supporting the shell. TOP RIGHT: early withdrawal. Both eye stalks physically invaginate down into the head; only short rounded closed stalk nubs remain, no eyeballs floating elsewhere. The head lowers and folds backward toward the natural small opening at the lower FRONT-LEFT of the shell; a thick compact muscular fold shows the direction of retraction. Much of the forefoot remains grounded; tail shortens slightly. Shell and cargo stay in their original location. BOTTOM LEFT: late withdrawal. Face and eyes are entirely inside the front-left opening. Only a short thick rounded fold of mint muscle curls UP AND RIGHT into that entrance; the long forefoot has been drawn in, and a very small rear tail is still visible beneath the shell. This is physical retraction into the aperture, NOT uniform shrinking, melting, flattening, dismemberment, or changing the body into a separate curled worm. The shell begins to settle down only slightly as foot support disappears. BOTTOM RIGHT: final death pose, all head, eyestalks, muscular foot, and tail are fully withdrawn, with absolutely NO mint-white body outside. The same intact round golden shell and unchanged leaf-and-mushroom/berry cargo remain, lowered vertically ONLY until the shell's lowest golden edge contacts the former foot baseline y896. A subtle small dark front-left aperture with a natural golden rim is visible; do not cut a giant hole or arch through the shell, do not alter the spiral or add limbs. No lateral rolling, no changes in shell/cargo scale. Clear distinct silhouettes at every phase, clean transparent alpha, fully drawn complete creatures usable as animation source artwork. The motion is withdrawal followed by a short weighted settling of the rigid shell. Do not add motion trails, duplicates, translucent overlays, fade effects or ghosting.

assets.name: old-garden-snail
assets.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: actual production key-pose source drawings for a 2D game elder garden snail death animation. Image 1 is the only approved character design and registered neutral pose. Create a square 2048x2048 PNG with genuine transparent background, exactly 2x2 equal 1024x1024 cells, no gutters, border, grid lines, labels, captions, scenery, floor or cast shadows. Each cell is one complete SAME left-facing old garden snail at exactly the same pixel scale, camera, colors and shading. Map the supplied 512x512 reference uniformly 2x into each cell; the original foot baseline is y896 per 1024 cell. Preserve its amber-gold rounded spiral shell, three pale cream raised bands wrapping the shell, moss along the bands, the bent brown miniature bonsai trunk, its exact dark teal foliage clusters, pale ivory leaves, dangling orange-gold fruits, right-hand trailing vine, and original clean dark green outline. Preserve exact silhouette, proportions, scale, identity and original illustrated game art; never substitute mushrooms, red berries, a bag, or a different tree. Shell AND the whole moss/bonsai/vine garden are one rigid assembly: no scaling, squashing, stretching, new branches, missing foliage, rolling, or cargo rearrangement. Only the mint-ivory muscular snail body changes shape, through physical retraction into its natural small FRONT-LEFT shell opening. These four drawings, in reading order, show the required phases: TOP LEFT: exact neutral original, two upright eye stalks, round dark eyes, plump head, full soft foot and rear tail on baseline. TOP RIGHT: early withdrawal; both eye stalks have invaginated down into short closed nubs; head lowers and folds backward toward the front-left shell entrance, with visible thick soft muscle volume. Forefoot still grounded, rear tail slightly shorter, heavy shell/bonsai remain in original pose and position. BOTTOM LEFT: late withdrawal; face, eyes and stalks fully inside shell. A small thick rounded mint muscle fold curls UP AND RIGHT into that aperture. Long forefoot is gone and only a small rear tail remains. Physical pulling-in with clean occlusion, not a separate detached worm and not a uniformly shrinking flat foot. The rigid shell/garden begins settling down slightly as support disappears. BOTTOM RIGHT: final dead still pose; ALL soft body, head, eyes and tail entirely withdrawn. ONLY the same whole intact golden shell with pale bands and its exact moss, tree, fruits and trailing vine remains. This rigid assembly is translated vertically downward ONLY so the lowest golden shell edge rests on original y896 foot baseline. Preserve its full round shell volume and spiral; a small naturally rimmed dark opening at the lower front-left is visible, not a huge punched-out arch or cave. No mint-white body remains outside anywhere. All features fit comfortably inside each cell without clipping, clean transparent edges. The same death-motion language as a small bundle snail: eyestalks withdraw, body curls into shell, the heavy shell settles onto ground and stops. Elder garden snail should feel slow and weighty while static key drawings remain clear. Do not add tears, blood, skulls, particles, motion trails, ghosted duplicates, translucency or fade effects. All drawings will be used as real animation sources after approval.
